final_lessons: On this symbolic univariate task, a deeper 4-layer non-residual ReLU/GELU MLP with heavy layer norm can outperform shallow or residual variants by a lot.
For this dataset, depth with several layer norms beats shallow width; a 6x64 residual normalized MLP can greatly outperform 2-layer wide models.
When depth and width are strong, non-residual normalized MLPs can reach near-zero MSE, while comparable residual models are much worse.
Absent the strong non-residual normalized pattern, very wide/deep residual MLPs still perform well and beat shallow or narrow alternatives.
A non-residual 4x64 MLP with even partial layer norm is a near-zero-MSE architecture on this dataset.
Among residual-only choices, prefer the deepest width-64 model with multiple layer norms; narrow normalized residuals lag behind.
For residual MLPs here, width alone is weak without normalization; a 5x64 partially normalized model beats a 3x256 unnormalized one.
Deep wide non-residual MLPs with partial layer norm are consistently near-zero MSE, while shallow or narrow non-residual options can be poor.
When a 4x64 non-residual partially normalized MLP appears, it should be preferred over residual alternatives in this session.
Deep normalized residual 6x64 models are reliable winners over unnormalized residual or shallow non-residual choices when no strong non-residual normalized candidate is present.
